raw_response:
I've farmed these same 8 mu for 35 years now, so I know what works and what I can afford. My family has five mouths to feed, and my son works in a factory in town, so it's mostly me and my wife in the fields — we can't take big risks. If one crop fails, we don't eat.

For the winter wheat, I'll plant in early October like always. I saved some seed from last year, but I'll buy a few bags of improved seed from the village co-op to mix in — about 30 yuan per mu. For fertilizer, the extension guy says to put on more, but fertilizer is expensive and I don't have that kind of cash. Last year I used about one 50-jin bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, plus another half bag of urea topdressed in March when the wheat started jointing. That worked out fine — I got about 380 jin per mu. This year I'll do the same: roughly 14–15 kg of nitrogen per mu total, split between base and topdress. The soil is decent but not great, so I don't want to starve it, but I also can't go broke buying fertilizer.

I'll irrigate the wheat three times if I can afford the electricity for the pump — once before winter to help it establish, once at jointing in spring, and maybe once at heading if it stays dry. But if the pump bill gets too high, I might skip that last one. My neighbor Old Wang only irrigated twice last year and his wheat was okay, so I'll watch the weather. I spray herbicide in spring and keep some insecticide handy for aphids.

Maize is the busy one. Right after wheat harvest in early June, I have maybe a week to get the maize in the ground before it's too late. I hire a tractor to do quick rotary tillage, then plant the hybrid seed — you can't save hybrid seed, you have to buy new every year, about 50 yuan per mu. For fertilizer, I put down compound fertilizer at planting and then topdress with urea when the maize is at the big喇叭口 stage. That's about 12 kg of nitrogen per mu. I'll irrigate once or twice in summer if there's no rain — July usually brings some showers, so maybe just once at flowering if it looks dry. I spray herbicide right after planting and watch for maize borers.

I hire three days of labor for wheat harvest and two days for maize — my back isn't what it used to be at 53 — but mostly it's family work. Total cost will be around 4,400 yuan for everything, which is about what I can scrape together without borrowing. I'm hoping for 380 kg per mu on wheat and 420 kg on maize. Not trying to break records — I just need a steady year so my family eats and has a little cash left over.
